archetypes.name: sentinel-chain
archetypes.rationale: The plan maps every folded sentinel write to a specific host fence and ordering position; an incomplete or misordered chain causes resume-routing failures that are hard to debug at runtime.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each sentinel (step-1c through step-6) listed in the plan's folded-write table, verify that the named host fence exists in the scope files and would logically run before the corresponding step's work begins. Check that every code path through the step graph writes that sentinel exactly once, or that all writes are provably idempotent. Pay special attention to step-1e (must appear in both the Step 2a entry fence and the Step 3 entry fence) and step-5c (written only when PLAN_WRITE_OK=true). Flag any step whose sentinel write is implied by plan prose but has no concrete host fence named in the plan. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-claim-mapping
archetypes.rationale: The plan states specific new/updated assertions for test-design-structure.sh and test-design-pause-resume.sh; behavioral claims without a corresponding named assertion produce silent coverage gaps that allow regressions past CI.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each behavioral claim in the plan (folded writes, deleted preludes, idempotent multi-writes, negative guards, pause-load clearing, route-specific resume), confirm a corresponding named assertion or negative guard is described in the plan's test sections for test-design-structure.sh and test-design-pause-resume.sh. Identify any plan claim that has no stated test coverage, such as the HARD zero-sketch degraded branch writing both step-2a and step-2a.5, or the Gate A direct-to-Step-3 step-1e placement. Also check whether any assertion described in the test-plan sections contradicts a behavioral claim stated elsewhere in the plan. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: pause-protocol-safety
archetypes.rationale: The pause/resume protocol is the most operationally sensitive invariant; the plan modifies it in several places and any ordering or clearing mistake produces a silent skip-or-replay bug that surfaces only on interrupted runs.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review every point where the plan modifies or depends on the pause protocol: the design-pause-load.sh restore-then-clear-pause-requested contract, the folded-sentinel-before-pause-check invariant across all host fences, and the Step 6 deliberate after-pause exception. For each, check whether the stated contract is complete and whether the test plan verifies the before/after state (e.g., assert marker exists in snapshot before load; assert absent in live DESIGN_TMPDIR after load). Verify that no resumed path can encounter a gate check before its required folded sentinels are written. Also check that the Step 6 after-pause exception is described narrowly enough that an implementer cannot inadvertently replicate it in other fences. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
